scenario: Two avalanche-forecasting models, AvaX and AvaY, are evaluated on correct-forecast rates across complex high-relief terrain and simple low-relief terrain. AvaX is predominantly tested on complex terrain; AvaY mostly on simple terrain.

data.description: forecast accuracy rates by terrain complexity and entity

question: (a) Which entity has the higher aggregate forecast accuracy rate? (b) Which entity performs better within each terrain complexity stratum? (c) Compute each entity's corrected rate using a 50/50 terrain complexity mix. (d) Which entity should be preferred, and why does the aggregate ranking mislead?

ground_truth.explanation: Model AvaY's higher aggregate is driven by its disproportionate assignment to easier simple low-relief cases. Model AvaX outperforms Model AvaY in both terrain complexity strata. Standardising to a 50/50 terrain complexity mix gives Model AvaX 0.845 vs Model AvaY 0.8; Model AvaX is the superior performer once terrain complexity class is controlled.

naive_answer: Model AvaY is better because its aggregate forecast accuracy rate (0.87) exceeds Model AvaX's (0.7925).
naive_trap: Terrain complexity class is a confounder: Model AvaX handles the majority of harder complex high-relief cases, depressing its aggregate while Model AvaY benefits from easier cases.
reasoning_trace: (1) Complex high-relief: Model AvaX 0.77 > Model AvaY 0.7. (2) Simple low-relief: Model AvaX 0.92 > Model AvaY 0.9. (3) Model AvaX handles 85.0% complex high-relief cases vs Model AvaY's 15.0% — this pulls Model AvaX's aggregate down. (4) Corrected 50/50: Model AvaX=0.5×0.77+0.5×0.92=0.845; Model AvaY=0.5×0.7+0.5×0.9=0.8. Model AvaX wins after standardisation.
python_verification:
nA1,rA1,nA2,rA2 = 680,0.77,120,0.92
nB1,rB1,nB2,rB2 = 120,0.7,680,0.9
ovA=(nA1*rA1+nA2*rA2)/(nA1+nA2); ovB=(nB1*rB1+nB2*rB2)/(nB1+nB2)
assert ovB > ovA, 'naive: Model AvaY aggregate higher'
cA=0.5*rA1+0.5*rA2; cB=0.5*rB1+0.5*rB2
assert abs(cA-0.845)<0.005 and abs(cB-0.8)<0.005
assert cA > cB, 'corrected: Model AvaX wins'
